where.claim: Patient-specific contact recruitment priors are stable across chronological train-heldout splits and account for the established patient-mean early-ictal field association.

how.claim: Ordered within-event history contains a small short-range increment for next-contact choice beyond the unordered prefix; the identifiable increment is concentrated in the current and preceding rank sets.

when.claim: The event-reset within-event model does not test real-time seizure entry.

allowed_claim: A stable patient-specific contact recruitment scaffold is supplemented by a small, short-range within-event ordered transition correction. This correction is concentrated in the current and preceding rank sets and is not established as a unique recurrent mechanism, a real-time seizure state, or an incremental predictor of the patient-mean early-ictal field.
forbidden_claims: The RNN recovered a biological seizure manifold.
The learned rank-step persistence is a biological time constant.
Ordered within-event history predicts seizure timing.
The ordered residual independently explains early-ictal recruitment.
The selected model was independently confirmed in both datasets.
A two-dimensional brain state was identified from the Hankel spectrum.
next_action: Freeze the within-event architecture search. If pursued, build a separate IEI-aware inter-event study only after constructing a reliable seizure-specific 1-150 Hz early-ictal residual target.
